# kipple

> kipple is an MIT macOS command-line disk cleaner for caches and leftovers from AI coding tools, local models and developer toolchains under the home folder. Every command is a dry run unless --apply is given, the only destination is the Trash, and every move is recorded in a receipt that kipple restore can undo. Built to be driven by agents.

## CLI contract

- Every command accepts --json. With --json, stdout is exactly one JSON document; progress, warnings and errors go to stderr. Errors are also printed on stdout as {"error":{"code":"...","message":"..."}}.
- Exit codes: 0 success, 1 error, 2 usage error, 3 nothing to do, 4 partial (some items skipped or failed; each skip has a machine-readable reason).
- No command prompts when --json is set or stdout is not a terminal. --apply is the consent.
- Flow: `kipple scan --json > plan.json` (inspect items: id, rule, tier, path, allocated_bytes, selected, reasons) -> `kipple explain <id> --json` -> `kipple clean --json --only <id,...>` (dry run) -> `kipple clean --apply --json --only <id,...>` (result has receipt_id) -> `kipple history --json` -> `kipple restore <receipt_id> --json`, then `--apply` to undo.
- Item IDs are 12 characters, derived from rule ID and home-relative path; stable across runs.
- --only selects review and manual items (naming one is consent to its tier); info items are never moved. Anything else blocking an item (too_recent, git_dirty, contains_protected, owner_running, ...) still skips it.
- `kipple clean --plan plan.json --apply --json` treats a saved plan as untrusted candidates and re-checks them against a fresh scan.
- `kipple schema plan|receipt|rules|result` prints the JSON Schema, generated from the encoding types. schema_version is 1 and stays 1 within a kipple major version.
- `kipple tui` is interactive only (needs a terminal; with --json it is a usage error).
- KIPPLE_HOME and KIPPLE_STATE_DIR point kipple at a fixture home and receipts folder for tests; kipple refuses a KIPPLE_HOME that is, contains or is inside the real home.

## Safety rules

- Dry run is the only default; the Trash is the only destination. --permanent is refused (usage error, exit 2) in v0.1.0.
- One policy function approves every path; apply re-checks policy, rule conditions and item identity (dev, ino) immediately before each move.
- Hard-coded denylist (Documents, Desktop, Pictures, Mail, Messages, Photos, keychains, Preferences, cloud storage, .ssh, .gnupg, .aws, .env files, agent history, memory, plans and skills, ...). Config may add protections, never remove them.
- Never outside the home folder, never on another disk, never through a symbolic link, never as root, no sudo, no network, no telemetry.
- Moving into ~/.Trash needs Full Disk Access; without it kipple uses Apple's Trash API (receipt mover "nsfilemanager"), else it stops with error code trash_access. kipple restore --apply always needs Full Disk Access.
